# 39 — The Lynx 4.1 upgrade

What moved, what broke, what got fixed upstream, and what 3.9 → 4.1 makes
newly possible. Everything here was checked against the published packages or
measured on a build — nothing is taken from a release note alone.

## Two version axes, and why they don't match

"Lynx 4.1" is the **engine** version (`lynx-family/lynx`, tag `4.1.0`,
released 2026-09-07). The npm toolchain has its own, unrelated numbers. The
only npm package that tracks the engine is `@lynx-js/types`, which this repo
does not depend on — its element and event surfaces are hand-curated
(see [18 — Typed templates](18-typed-templates.md)).

So "update to 4.1" means two separate things:

| | what it is | what this upgrade did |
|---|---|---|
| **Toolchain** | the `@lynx-js/*` npm packages you build with | bumped to the current release train (table below) |
| **`targetSdkVersion`** | the engine floor stamped into the bundle | **left at 3.2** — see below |
| **Engine / Explorer** | what runs the bundle on device | your install; 4.1.0 is downloadable |

### `targetSdkVersion` stays at 3.2, deliberately

`LynxTemplatePlugin`'s default is `targetSdkVersion: '3.2'` and
`pluginAngularLynx` has never overridden it, which is why nothing in this repo
has ever hit a version-compatibility error. A bundle runs on its declared
engine version **and every later one**, so a 3.2 bundle already runs fine on
4.0 and 4.1; raising it to `'4.1'` would only *narrow* compatibility (a 4.1
bundle refuses to load on a 4.0 engine with fatal error
[10204](https://lynxjs.org/next/api/errors/error-code.html#10204-e_app_bundle_load_parse_failed)).

Nothing this repo uses is gated behind a higher `targetSdkVersion`. New
*elements* aren't gated by it either — `<video>` works on a 4.1 engine
regardless of what the bundle declares. The one thing that does need a raise is
the `lynx.fetchBundle` lazy-bundle loader (`engineVersion: '3.9'` or higher). See
[Lynx's compatibility guide](https://lynxjs.org/next/guide/compatibility.html).

## What actually broke

### 1. Lazy routes stopped shipping their chunk (production only)

The only real regression, and a nasty one because **dev builds hide it**.

Since `@lynx-js/template-webpack-plugin@0.13` an **unnamed** dynamic
`import()` is treated as a Lynx *lazy bundle* rather than an ordinary async JS
chunk. Measured on `examples/router`, before and after:

```
rspeedy 0.15  →  dist/static/js/async/171.2e1eef3845.js        ← the chunk
                 dist/static/js/async/171.449215acaf.web.js
                 dist/main.{lynx,web}.bundle

rspeedy 0.17  →  dist/lazy-bundle/…b7e285253ba97ddd.bundle     ← new
                 dist/main.{lynx,web}.bundle
                                                                ← chunk gone
```

The chunk is renamed into the per-bundle intermediate directory, then
`LynxEncodePlugin` force-inlines every manifest chunk of a lazy bundle
(`appType === 'DynamicComponent'` bypasses `inlineScripts`) and deletes the
inlined assets. The app-service still asks for `static/js/async/…`, so the
route 404s at navigation time. The delete is gated on `!isDev`, so only
production builds are affected.

**Fixed** in `pluginAngularLynx` by tapping the template plugin's own public
`asyncChunkName` hook and returning `''`, which reproduces the pre-0.13 state
at all three places that consult it. That hook only runs for *named* chunk
groups, so each lazy `import()` now needs a `webpackChunkName` comment — and an
unnamed one under `asyncChunks: true` **fails the build** with an error naming
the import, instead of silently shipping a broken bundle. Full write-up in
[15 — Routing](15-routing.md).

Blast radius: `asyncChunks` defaults to `false`, and `examples/router` is the
only app in the repo that turns it on.

### 2. A latent write race in the intermediates started firing

`verify:dynamic-component-build` began failing intermittently with
`SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'if'`. One `rspeedy build` compiles the `lynx`
and `web` environments **in parallel into the same `dist/`**, and both were
writing `.rspeedy/<entry>/background.js` and `main-thread.js` — the same paths.
Whichever finished last won, or the two interleaved into a torn file. The bump
didn't introduce the race, it shifted the timings enough to expose it.

The shipped bundles were never affected (each environment's template plugin
packs the assets it holds in memory, not what's on disk); only tools that
*read* the intermediates saw it. Fixed with a `.web` infix, the same pattern
already used for async chunks and hot-update files.

### 3. Nothing else

Checked and found **not** to apply:

- **`dev.client` removed in rspeedy 0.17.** It was rspeedy's own top-level
  `Dev.client` (the pre-`LynxWebSocketModule` `websocketTransport` shim) that
  went away. `environments.lynx.dev.client.overlay`, which this plugin does
  set, is rsbuild's — still present in `@rsbuild/core@2.2.4`'s
  `AllowedEnvironmentDevKeys`. No change needed.
- **Intermediates moved `.rspeedy/` → `.lynx/`.** That's the template
  plugin's *default*; `pluginAngularLynx` passes `intermediate` explicitly, so
  the layout is unchanged and every script and doc that references
  `dist/.rspeedy/` still holds.
- **`beforeEncode`/`afterEncode` hooks changed `entryNames` → `chunkGroups`.**
  This repo taps neither.
- **Preact 11 in `@lynx-js/react@0.126`.** Only
  `@lynx-js/react/worklet-runtime` is consumed here; Angular is the renderer.
  `verify:worklet` and `verify:gesture` pass.
- **`@lynx-js/react` 0.123 requires `template-webpack-plugin@^0.13`.** Both
  moved together.

## The console sweep

Every one of the 22 examples was then run in the web preview and its console
read. Three real problems surfaced — none of them caused by the bump, all of
them fixed here — and after that **all 22 boot clean**.

### 1. The web preview's assets were cross-origin (so was its dev socket)

rspeedy's dev `assetPrefix` is an absolute LAN-IP origin, so a phone on the
same Wi-Fi can fetch assets. The **`web` environment never runs on the phone**
— it runs in a browser tab opened at `localhost`, where that prefix makes every
asset a cross-origin subresource that the dev server's
`Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp` then blocks. One cause, two
long-standing symptoms:

- `<video>`, `<image>` and `<svg src>` appeared broken in the web preview.
  `examples/media` and `examples/primitives` both documented this as an
  unavoidable artifact with "open the preview at the printed LAN-IP URL" as the
  workaround.
- `dev-reload-client.ts` resolves its WebSocket against
  `__webpack_require__.p`, so it dialled the LAN IP from a localhost page,
  failed, and retried forever — **~50 `WebSocket connection … failed` errors
  per boot**, which is what was burying everything else.

`pluginAngularLynx` now scopes `dev.assetPrefix` to `http://localhost:<port>/`
for the `web` environment only (`<port>` is rsbuild's own placeholder,
substituted with the port actually bound). `lynx` keeps the LAN-IP prefix it
needs. A bare `'/'` would be the natural value but the Lynx build engine's
`printUrls` does `new URL()` on it and throws.

Measured after: `examples/primitives`' SVG file renders (then a capybara drawing, since replaced by `lynx-classes.svg`), and
`examples/media` shows a decoded video frame with `error 0×`.

### 2. `ng-lynx-capture` was broken, so hello-world's IFR never hydrated

`examples/hello-world` logged `first-screen snapshot did NOT match the real
first render` on every boot. The chain:

1. `bin/capture-first-screen.mjs` didn't `define` `__HAS_FIRST_SCREEN__` or
   `__ENABLE_SELECTOR_QUERIES__`, added to the runtime after that file was
   written. Both are read at module scope, so the capture bundle threw
   `ReferenceError` instead of degrading — `npm run capture` failed outright.
2. The wire protocol later gained string interning.
3. With no working capture, the committed `first-screen.json` stayed in the
   **pre-interning** format and could never match.

Fixed by defining all three constants in the capture bin and re-capturing. The
console now reads `first-screen snapshot matched — hydrated in place`. See
[20 — First screen](20-first-screen.md).

### 3. `LynxSlider` measured its track before the element existed

`[lynx-web] cannot find from for selector [ng-ref-30]`, logged as an **error**
by web-core on every slider mount. `measureTrack()` ran from `ngAfterViewInit`,
which is *inside* change detection — before `LynxRendererFactory2.end()` has
flushed anything, so it queried an element the Main Thread had not been told
about. Harmless by design (`fail` is a no-op; the `touchstart` re-measure is
the real guarantee) but alarming and noisy.

Now hops a microtask and awaits `whenFlushed()` — the barrier the runtime
already exports for exactly this. On device the best-effort measurement now
runs against a materialised tree instead of racing one.

### What's left, and why none of it is ours

Four lines appear in every app and are all `@lynx-js/web-core`'s own:

| line | source |
|---|---|
| the `LYNX WEB PLATFORM` ASCII banner, `{0: Object, 1: Object, 2: Object}` | web-core boot logging |
| `An iframe which has both allow-scripts and allow-same-origin…` | the `__web_preview` page from `@lynx-js/web-rsbuild-server-middleware` |
| `using deprecated parameters for the initialization function` | wasm-bindgen glue inside web-core's own client bundle |
| `[HMR] No 'window.document' found, CSS HMR disabled` | informational — the background bundle runs in a Worker |

## What got fixed upstream (and is now worth re-testing)

Several standing "web preview can't do this" notes in these docs were written
against `web-core@0.21`. The releases in between claim to close some of them.
What has been checked against the published packages, and what still needs a
live run:

| claim in the docs | upstream change | status |
|---|---|---|
| `lynx.createIntersectionObserver` unimplemented on web ([24](24-visibility.md)) | web-core 0.25.0 adds it (#3383) | works, live in `examples/router`, after a runtime fix |
| `main-thread:gesture` / `__SetGestureDetector` unimplemented ([32](32-gestures.md)) | web-core 0.26.0 adds **no-op** detector APIs (#3743) so the page renders | still a no-op |
| `nativeApp.getFields is not a function` ([09](09-forms.md), [10](10-element-queries.md), [37](37-ui-gallery.md)) | not mentioned in any changelog | still missing |
| `textarea` rendered as a bare HTML `<textarea>`, so `bindinput` never fired | web-core 0.23.0 maps it to `x-textarea` (#2971) | not re-run |
| `<frame auto-height>` broken on web | web-core 0.23.0 fixes it | not re-run |

Also new on web, none of it previously available:

- `__AddEventListener` / `__RemoveEventListener` element PAPIs (0.24.0) —
  binds a main-thread **function** as a listener, as opposed to `__AddEvent`'s
  handler *name*. The changelog says this exists specifically for "cards that
  build their UI directly from the Element PAPIs", which is exactly what
  ng-lynx is.
- `lynx.getEngine()` (0.24.0) — the main-thread Engine context proxy
  (`__RenderPage` / `__UpdatePage` / `__DestroyLifetime` /
  `__UpdateGlobalProps`), again aimed at PAPI-built cards.
- `__GetComputedStyleByKey` (0.23.1) and `__GetAttributeNames` (0.24.1).
- A `scroll-view` mouse-drag plugin (0.26.0) — opt-in via
  `import '@lynx-js/web-core/plugins/scroll-view-mouse-drag'`, which would make
  scrollers behave like touch in the web preview instead of needing a wheel.
- `enableCSSInheritance` for text inside views, gradient text included (0.26.1).

## What the engine gained in 3.9 → 4.1

Taken from `lynx-family/lynx-website`'s `packages/lynx-compat-data`, filtered
to `version_added` on android/ios. There are **no removals and no JS-API
changes** anywhere in that range — the additions are all elements, element
attributes, and one CSS feature.

### 4.1

- **`<video>`** — `version_added: 4.1`, android + ios, marked experimental.
  Attributes `src`/`loop`/`volume`/`muted`/`speed`/`object-fit`/`mode`/
  `timeupdate-interval`, nine events, and `play`/`pause`/`stop`/`seek`.

  **This resolves a standing open question in this repo.** `examples/media`
  and `examples/primitives` both record `LynxCreateUIException: video ui not
  found` on an Explorer recorded as 4.0.0 (really engine 3.7, see below),
  concluded as "needs a host app that registers the video UI". The real
  reason is simpler: **the element did not exist before 4.1**. On Explorer
  4.1.0 it should just work, with no host-app changes.
- `ios-pan-intercept-gesture-class` / `-view-class` / `-view-tag` on every
  element (ios) — intercept another platform gesture recognizer by class.
  The nested-scroll fix this repo needed turned out to be older:
  `pan-intercept-direction` + `pan-intercept-scope` (iOS 3.4, Android 3.6),
  measured working on engine 3.7 in `ui-gallery`'s Draggable demo, which no
  longer toggles `[enable-scroll]`. See
  [32 — Gestures](32-gestures.md#a-drag-inside-a-scroll-view-pan-intercept-).
  All five attributes are typed.
- `scroll-view` gains `contentsizechanged` (ios). Android has had it since
  1.5, and it's already typed on `<scroll-view>`. It doesn't apply to
  `examples/list`'s stale-status workaround after all: that page is a
  `<list>`, not a `<scroll-view>`.
- `<svg current-color>` (ios) — relevant to the narrowed SVG-fill finding in
  `examples/primitives` (CSS-class fills render black; presentation-attribute
  fills work).
- `scroll-view.takeContentScreenshot` / `takeScreenshot` (ios),
  `page.takeScreenshot` (android + ios), `textarea.takeScreenshot`.
- `<overlay android-navigation-bar-style>` (android),
  `<blur-view ios-user-interface-style>` (ios).

### 4.0

- **`@media` queries** — native platforms (the web preview drops them).
  Needs `pluginLynxConfig({ enableCSSRule: true })`, and a bundle built that
  way crashes engines before 4.0, so raise `targetSdkVersion`. See
  [13 — Styling](13-styling.md#media-queries) and `examples/responsive`.
- **`<blur-view>`** and **`<webview>`** — both `version_added: 4.0`,
  android + ios, with full attribute/event/method surfaces.
- `features.autolink` (android + ios).
- `<input default-value>` / `<textarea default-value>` (android),
  `markdown.getCharIndexByPoint` (android + ios),
  `list.experimental-search-ref-anchor-strategy`.

### 3.9

- **`<scroll-coordinator>`** and **`<viewpager>`** — both `version_added: 3.9`,
  android + ios, with their full surfaces.
- `<frame bindloadmetrics>`, `<frame enable-multi-async-thread>`.

> ✅ **The "open contradiction" is resolved: the Explorer was engine 3.7.**
> `examples/primitives` recorded `scroll-coordinator`, `viewpager`,
> `blur-view` and `webview` all throwing `ui not found` on "Explorer 4.0.0",
> though the compat data puts them at 3.9/4.0. Measured on 2026-10-16: that
> Explorer logs `lynx sdk version: 3.7` for every bundle, and both copies on
> this machine were installed in June, before 4.0.0 shipped. All four, plus
> `<refresh>` (3.8) and `<video>` (4.1), are newer than 3.7. Separately,
> web-core 0.26.1 now renders `webview`, `blur-view`, `viewpager`, `refresh`
> and `scroll-coordinator` in the web preview (measured in
> `examples/primitives`).

## `@lynx-js/genui` 0.0.6 → 0.4.0

Held back at first, on the assumption that four minors of new surface would
need real work. That was **measured, and the assumption was wrong** — it is a
drop-in, so it landed on this branch too.

Evidence, with zero code changes: `tsc -p tsconfig.json` clean, `ngc` build
clean, all **54 harnesses** pass (the four genui ones included), and
`examples/genui` renders identically in the web preview — 118 elements, same
content, clean console. The OpenUI half was not click-verified in the browser
(Lynx's own event dispatch can't be driven by a synthetic DOM `TouchEvent`);
`verify:genui-openui` and `verify:genui-openui-runtime` are what cover it.

It's a no-op because this repo consumes only `a2ui/store`, `a2ui/functions`,
`a2ui-catalog-extractor` and `a2ui-prompt`. Diffing the published tarballs: the
`exports` map is purely additive except one rename nothing here imports
(`openui/styles/renderer.css` → `theme.css`), and the only type change in the
whole `a2ui/store` surface is `Signal` moving from `@preact/signals` to the new
`@lynx-js/react-signals` — harmless, because `runtime/src/genui/` deliberately
uses **Angular's** `Signal` and its own subscription set rather than adopting
Preact signals.

`peerDependencies` deliberately stays at `>=0.0.6`: the runtime type-checks and
runs against both, so narrowing it would restrict consumers for no reason.

Two consequences to know about, neither a blocker:

- **A new peer, `@lynx-js/lynx-ui >= 3.133.0`**, is declared by 0.4.0 and is
  *not* installed — pnpm emitted no warning and nothing here needs it. It would
  only matter for the `openui/catalog/*` components this repo doesn't use.
- **`@openuidev/lang-core` gains install-time telemetry.** 0.4.0 widens the
  range to `^0.2.11`, which resolves to 0.2.18, and 0.2.18 adds
  `postinstall: node ./postinstall.cjs` — pseudonymous install telemetry to
  PostHog (salted project id, tool/OS metadata, the IP PostHog observes). The
  previously pinned 0.2.9 has none. Opt out with `OPENUI_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1`
  or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` — both workflows now set `DO_NOT_TRACK: '1'` at workflow
  level (see [36 — CI](36-ci.md)); local installs are not covered.

What the upgrade brings, all additive: the MCP Apps protocol and an A2UI
`McpApp` catalog component that embeds trusted bundles through `<frame>`; 26
individually-importable `openui/catalog/*` entries plus
`createOpenUiLibrary({ includeDefaultComponents: false })` and
`openui/explicit`, so unselected built-ins stay out of the static graph; a Lynx
XML playground and a reusable Lynx XML system-prompt builder; `xxs`/`2xl` gap
sizes; lynx-ui primitives and Luna theme tokens for the OpenUI controls; and a
1.8 MB win — `a2ui/styles/theme.css` was 99.9% one base64 Material Icons TTF
that every catalog component dragged in, now split into
`a2ui/styles/material-icons.css` and pulled only by `Icon`/`DateTimeInput`.
